title: #12 The Conquest Of Iraq

مضَّك الله ملكة "هذا ولله صم الساعة" "بسم الله" ألذي لا يضرُّ ما إسمه شيءٌ في ألسموات والأرض "بسم الله" "وَإِذْ جَعَلْنَا الْبَيْتَ مَثَابَةً لِّلنَّاسِ وَأَمْنًا"

فسلك الطريق لم يسلقها إنسانٌ قبلهم قط وسارع إلى مكة في طريق لم يسلق قبله قط وتعتله في ذالك أمرٌلم يقعل لغيره فجعل يسير متعصفًا على غير جاد حتى إنتهاء إلى المكة

english:
Lessons from the Haroob(حروب) of Ar-Riddah(ردَّة), we're done with the Riddah(ردَّة) wars, the wars of the apostasy.

Some lessons to be learned from that.

Number one, that Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه made Islam distinguished from all other.

And he refused to allow Islam to be contaminated with Shirk(شرك).

Religion in its early stage is very susceptible to change.

So it was very critical for Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه to ensure that Islam, during that critical stage does not change from the way it was left when Rasool Allah ﷺ passed away.

And that's why Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) as we mentioned in a statement, he said; The revelation has stopped, meaning Jibreel(جِبْرِيْل) will not come and fix our mistakes, now.

Jibreel(جِبْرِيْل) is not going to descend after the death of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

And the religion is complete.

So I'm not going to allow to diminish, while I'm alive I am not going to allow the religion of Islam to go down when I'm still alive.

And it would be an interesting research to study a comparison between the early stage of Islam and the early stage of Christianity and the involvement of government in the development of the religion because

government does have a role, on how religion is practiced.

So one cannot rule out the influence of government on the practice of religion.

And that was true even in the time of Khulafa Ar-Rashidoon(خلفاء ألراشدون) it's true today and it was true with every religion.

With Christianity, there was a lot of involvement from the government side, in the development of the religion.

So the Christianity that we have today, there is a strong influence of early Roman Empire government in how the religion reached to the stage, it is in now.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه was now digging the roots for the Islamic government and the way it will rule over Islam and he's setting the ground rules; as I mentioned to you earlier.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه wanted to ensure that the people, who already became Muslim would practice the same Islam they were practicing in the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ,

and I'm not willing to compromise even on a saddle of a horse or a string of a camel, a rope that you would tie to the camels neck.

He said: I'm not going to forgive them even on a rope tied to a camels neck that they used to pay it to Rasool Allah ﷺ.

And Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) through a severe battle and conflict, was able to enforce the law of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ on the people, who were already Muslim before.

So by the end of the Riddah(ردَّة) wars, everybody in Arabia came to the conclusion that our Islam will be, the Islam in the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ

and it will continue as it is and we will have no say, in changing it.

He also purified the Peninsula from Shirk(شرك) and he established the Hukm(حكم) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ on everyone, equally.

Number two: He purified the peninsula and made it a launchpad for the conquest that would come later on.

Because you cannot start an expansion unless you have a base and that base needs to be strong, if the conquest will continue.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه wanted to make sure that the bastion of Islam, the base would be cleaned from all forms of Shirk(شرك) and that it will be a strong Jama'ah(جماعة)

that abides by the law and follows the Ameer(أمير).

So it is ready to move on and start spreading the religion to the corners of the earth.

And he succeeded in doing that after the Huroob(حروب) of Ar-Riddah(ردَّة).

Number three, the wars of Riddah(ردَّة) were an opportunity for the Khalifah(خليفه) to know the characteristics of men.

Because you only know people in time of conflict in time of peace and security everybody can claim to be everything.

And that's why in time of peace, the Munafiqeen(مُنافقين) stick their heads out.

In the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ, when there's a truce or a lull in war the Munafiqeen(مُنافقين) would be the loudest in the streets.

And then as soon as conflict breaks out, they go underground and you can't see them anymore.

So you can't really tell the quality of the people, until you put them in the Fitnah(فِتْنَه), in the Balla(بلاء), in the trials, and that's where the reality of what's inside comes out.

So the Huroob(حروب) of Ar-Riddah(ردَّة) were an opportunity for As-Siddique(ألصديق) to know, who was a true believer and who was a false believer.

Do people think that they will claim to be believers and they will not go through Fitnah(فِتْنَه) and then Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ says, So, Allah will know who are true in their claims, and who are lying.

Everybody is saying that we're Muslim we're believers, but the Fitnah(فِتْنَه) will determine, who is true in their claim and who's not.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) knew the quality of the people through the Huroob(حروب) of Ar-Riddah(ردَّة).

And that helped him in his choice of leaders.

So it was actually a training course for the leaders of the future.

The ones, who played the most important role in fighting the Riddah(ردَّة) continue to be the same ones, who will spread the religion to the empires of the day.

Number four, it was the practical Fiqh(فقه) of Riddah(ردَّة), there were Ayaat(آيات) in Qur'an and Ahadith(احاديث) in Sunnah(سنة) that talked about Riddah(ردَّة),

but it's remained the theoretical concept, because it didn't actually happen in Madina.

In the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ, and there was no actual Riddah(ردَّة) in the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ, so it was Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), who taught us how to understand

the Ayaat(آيات) and Ahadith(احاديث) of Rasool Allah ﷺ relating to Riddah(ردَّة).

Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) and many of the Sahabah(صحابه) did not understand the meaning of the Hadith(حديث), It was Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), who told them, what it means.

So now, the base was ready to send out the armies to spread out the Da'wah(دعوة) of Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So now we're going to start talking about the conquests of Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه and we'll start with the conquest of Iraq.

Ghazwa Al-Iraq(غزوة العراق) or Fath Al-Iraq(فتح العراق) - the opening of Iraq.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa Ash-Shaibani(ألمثنى بن حارثه ألشعيباني) from Bannu Shaiban(بنوشعيبان), from Iraq, he came to the Khalifah(خليفه) and he proposed to him an idea that was already appealing to the Khalifah(خليفه) and he was thinking about it.

He told him; I want you to give me authority and appoint me over my people in my area to wage war against the enemies of Allah in Iraq.

Iraq was part of the Persian Empire.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه approved his proposal.

So now Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) does not have to send an army, Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه), all what he wants from Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is to get legitimacy for his position,

which he already had, he was a chief of his tribe, and to fight with his own people against the enemy of Allah.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه agreed.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) started now, using the Karr(كرَءّ) and Far(فر) the attack and retreat method of fighting against the Persian armies

because of the small group he has; he can't afford a fixed march ahead to fight the enemy in large confrontation.

So he has used the method of Karr Wal Farr(كرء والفر) you ambush the enemy in one place and then you retreat and then you attack in another place and use the method of surprising the enemy.

Because of the small group that he had, he could afford this fast mobility and it was also more protective for him and his group rather than

have a fixed base, from which to fight from.

Now, keep in mind that Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is someone we already talked about we talked about early on in this series.

When Rasool Allah ﷺ was in Makkah searching for support he was searching for somebody to give him support.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه told him: These are good people, strong men let's go and talk to them.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه went and spoke and he presented the message of Rasool Allah ﷺ.

So, they asked Rasool Allah ﷺ to speak and he recited some Ayaat(آيات) of Qur'an and they said: We like this very much and these are words of truth

and a people, who have fought you because of this are an evil people, meaning the people of Quraish(قُرَيْشْ).

You remember that conversation?

And then Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) what did he say? He said; We can offer you support from one side, but we cannot offer you support from the other side.

We can offer you support from the side of the Arabs but we cannot offer you support from other side of the Persians because we cannot fight them, we cannot stand up and fight the Persian Empire.

But things have changed now and Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is a Muslim and he is the one, who's coming to the Khalifah(خليفه) and urging him

to allow him to fight against them, see how Islam changes the heart.

And if Islam does not bring that change, then there's a problem in the understanding of the person of Islam.

Because with the Sahara(سحرة) of Firaun(فرعون), who were willing to stand up against the Nabi(نَبِي) of Allah for a small amount of money.

Are you going to pay us, are going to give us something, if we win?

Firaun(فرعون) said: Yes, I'm gonna pay you a lot and I will make you very close to me.

But when they became believers, these people, who're doing it for money.

Now, when Firaun(فرعون) said: I'm going to kill you, they would said: We would rather die than give up our religion.

So instantaneously Eeman(ايمان) made them not only give up money, but give up their lives for Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So that's the transformational power that Eeman(ايمان) should have.

So Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is saying that I want you to give me authority and I will do it.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه did give Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) that authority and he started out the conquest in Iraq.

There was a member of his people, this was a big tribe Bannu Shaiban(بنوشعيبان) and they belong to Rabiyyah(ربيعة), one of them, his name is Mad'oor Bin Udae(مذعور بن عدي)

he was competing with Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) over the position of leading the effort.

And he sent a letter to Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه and he said; We are Ahlaas Al-Khail(أحلاس ألخيل), Ahlaas Al-Khail(أحلاس ألخيل) means, we're stuck to the backs of our horses.

In other words, we ride our horses so much we're so trained in it, we're so good at it.

We're Fursan As-Sabah(فرسان ألصباح), and we are the Knights of the morning.

We attack our enemies early in the morning, and I have men with me, each one of them is equal to a 100.

And he is asking Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) to appoint him as a leader over the Army's in that area.

So now Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) is dealing with a situation where he already appointed Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) and here's somebody else asking for the same position.

And Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) sent a letter to Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) saying that there's a man from my people who contended with me and try to take away my position or compete with me

in this role that you have appointed me to.

So, I just wanted to let you know about it.

Now, Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه is dealing with the realities of life.

You know, there are some interpersonal issues there are… it happens.

It happens even among Muslims, Muslims are not angels.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه he knows, how to run Jama'ah(جماعة) he knows how to manage the affairs of the social life of people and this is part of the ability of the leader.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه to solve this issue because he was already sending in Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to lead the entire enterprise.

He sent a letter to Mad'oor(مذعور), telling him I take your word for it, what you said.

Even though it might have been an exaggeration of his abilities Allah Ho Alam(ألله أعلم).

He said: I take your word for what you said and I believe you and I'm asking you to join hands with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and to be with him and to follow him, wherever he goes.

Rather than put Mad'oor(مذعور) and Muthanna(مثنى) in the same.

I mean, he could have told Mad'oor(مذعور) to go under the leadership of Muthanna(مثنى), whom I already appointed, he could have done that and some complications could have came out of that situation.

He said: No! You go with Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد).

So he separated between the two.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is leading an army and Mad'oor(مذعور) with his group are following the leadership of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد)

and nobody can contest the leadership with Khalid(خالد).

They all agree to the ability and the leadership of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) I mean, Sahabah(صحابه) of Rasool Allah ﷺ, who are earlier in Islam than him would all admit

that Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه is the most capable among us, in leading Armies.

What was the plan of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق)?

Al-Muthanna Bin Harisa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) played a role for some time.

But now, Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) wants to have a greater enterprise in the area of Iraq.

So his plan was to send two armies, one army to attack from the south east and the second army to attack from the northwest.

The army that would attacked from the south east was the army of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and he sent him a letter saying go on towards Iraq.

Because Khalid(خالد) was in Al-Yamamah(أليمامة) he just finished off the Harb(حرب) with was Musailimah Al-Kazzab(مسيلمة ألكذاب).

Go on towards Iraq, until you enter it began with the gateway to India, which is Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى), they used to call the area of Al-Basra(ألبصرة), they used to call it the gateway to India,

because anybody traveling to India would go through the Persian sea.

So they would call it the gateway to India, he said: And start from the gateway to India and Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) it is interesting as if Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه is seeing the map in front of him.

When there were no maps, in their hands.

He said: So you enter from the gateway to India, which is Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى) render that people of Persia and those nations under their rule peaceable.

And then he sent an army from the northwest, under the leadership of Ayyad Bin Ghanam(عياض بن غنم), one of the Sahabah رضي الله عنهم and he told him to attack from Al-Musayikh(ألمصيخ) which is the North West.

And then look at this strategic sense of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق).

He said: You both start attacking inwards into Iraq and try racing towards Al-Heira(ألحيرة) and whoever gets to Al-Heira(ألحيرة) first is the Ameer(أمير) over the other one.

Al-Heira(ألحيرة) was midway between Al-Ubullah(ألأبلَّى) and Al-Musayikh(ألمصيخ).

And Al-Heira(ألحيرة) is in a very strategic position.

It is very close to Al-Madain(ألمدائن) which is the capital of the Persian Empire, but it's towards the Arabian Peninsula side.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه wanted them to set base in a Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

So, the two armies attack from the north and the south.

They meet in Al-Heira(ألحيرة), they joined together and then they make their final hit at the Capital, which was a very strategic plan.

This is his letter, he said: When you have joined each other at Al-Heira(ألحيرة), have broken the defenses of Persia and are sure that the Muslims will not be attacked from behind.

Let one of you cover the Muslims and his comrade by staying at Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

Let the other attack Allah's enemy and your enemy in their own house and the abode of their power, Al-Madain(ألمدائن).

Masaleh Kisra(مصالح كسرى), the army base of Kisra(كسرى) was towards the south.

So it was the job of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) to take care of the army basis, and Ayyad Bin Ghanam(عياض بن غنم) will come from the desert side

and descend south, until they meet in Al-Heira(ألحيرة), whoever reaches Al-Heira(ألحيرة) first leads the other and then one of you stays behind and protects the rear of the army

So Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) in his way of fighting.

Whenever he gets a break through, he pursues it and he keeps on at the enemy's neck as far as he could go.

So his reputation was, Yani(يعني), the enemy used to have this terror from Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) because they know that even if they turn their backs,

he's not gonna allow them to leave.

So before they come to battle, their knees are already shaking.

When they hear the name of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and all of the stories about him swallowing poison, nothing happens to him and the rumors are going around that he has received a sword from heaven.

See, they misunderstood SaifUllah(سيف الله) because the name of Khalid(خالد) was SaifUllah(سيف الله) the sword of Allah.

What they understood is that he received a sword from God.

So in one battle with the Romans, they actually asked Khalid(خالد) to come forth and the leader of the army went to investigate this matter.

He asked Khalid(خالد), He said: Is it true that you are given by your Prophet a sword that came from God?

He said: No, that's not true.

It's just that the Prophet said that I am a sword of the swords of Allah.

He didn't lie, he told him the truth.

Now, this is an amazing story, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and his army are in Al-Firat(ألفرات), which is between Syria and Iraq, very faraway land.

He wants to go back to Iraq, he wants to go back to Al-Heira(ألحيرة).

That's where his base is, that's where he belongs, and he's made it huge distance now.

So he wants to go back.

So he sends his army and usually when you send an army and you're traveling long distance, you would break the army up, and it would have a rear army to protect the army that is ahead to protect it from behind

so the army is marching in two segments.

There's a separation between them could be hours, it could be days.

So he sends the major part of the army ahead, and then he has a small branch of the Army, marching behind it to protect it so that it wouldn't be ambushed from behind, especially that he just finished

fighting with the three powers of the area's the Arabs, Romans and the Persians.

He wants to make sure that the back is protected.

So they're traveling from the extreme west of Iraq or actually in Syria, to Al-Heira(ألحيرة), which is in the central area of Al-Iraq close to Karbala(كربلا), and Najaf(نجف).

So Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه is with the rear army.

Khalid(خالد) goes to his close friends, and he tells them, how about to make Hajj(حَجْ) this year?

And that was the season of Hajj(حَجْ).

And for those of you, who have been to Makkah, and who has seen Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه), Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) is like a magnet that draws you close to it wherever you are on the face of the earth.

If you visited the Al-Ka'aba(اَلْكَعْبَه) once you're addicted.

We have made the house of Allah Masabah(مثابة), Masabah(مثابة) is a place that you would always want to go back to, Yatuboo Alai(يطوبو عليه)

you want to go back to again and again.

You see it once, you're hooked for life, and people who have this feeling they start getting this feeling before Hajj(حَجْ), you know, like a person who's on drugs.

You feel that aching feeling whenever you see it.

So when the season of Hajj(حَجْ) comes, you feel it in your blood, you want to go there.

So, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) now, wants to go to Hajj(حَجْ), it's too late.

They're telling him what are you talking about, we're hundreds of miles away.

He said: Just believe me, let's go.

So he chooses this close group of his friends and they decide they're going to give it a shot and go to Hajj(حَجْ).

Now they have never enter Al-Firat(ألفرات) before they don't know the territory they have never traveled in that land ever before and they have no guide whatsoever.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) wants to give it a shot and try it out.

Khalid Ibn Walid رضي الله عنه you would assume that these things would come from a teenager.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) at the time was a mature old man.

But Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) was an enterpriser, an audacious person willing to take any risk, that was his personality, that was his makeup. Let's try!

It's time for Hajj(حَجْ). Let's give it a try!

So he doesn't tell anybody about the idea.

He only tells a few of the key members of the rear army.

He tells them we're gonna be absent for some time, we're going for Hajj(حَجْ).

Now they are heading in a direction they have no idea where they're going.

At-Tabari(ألطبري) says: They followed the path that was not walked by man before them at all.

Because you had such routes in the desert where people would travel and you'd have posts along the way to cater to the needs of people.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is now taking a route that hasn't been taken by anybody before him.

And he did something and Allah has given him Karamaat(كرامات) that happened to nobody before him.

At-Tabari(ألطبري) says: He was rushing recklessly going in a path that he doesn't know until it came out in Arafah(عرفة).

They just made their way through and At-Tabari(ألطبري) says: It was a reckless move.

I mean, they have no guide, they don't know their directions well, they just went ahead.

And these are veterans of war, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and the men around him.

They can handle such a situation but it was such a great risk.

They went, they made it to Arafah(عرفة) finish their Hajj(حَجْ).

Soon after, shaved their heads and sneaked out without telling anybody.

Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) only hears the news when he's back in Madina and he was very angry.

Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) rushes back and believe it or not, he makes it to the rear of the army before it gets into Al- Heira(ألحيرة).

So this army is traveling within Iraq, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) rushes makes Hajj(حَجْ) and goes back and hits the rear of his army and comes into Al- Heira(ألحيرة) as if nothing happened.

And nobody knew about it, except when they saw their heads were shaved.

What have you done?

Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), just imagine the feeling of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق), hearing the news that Khalid(خالد) deserted his army came and made Hajj(حَجْ) and goes back.

So I can only imagine the feeling of Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) it will be an ambivalent feeling of both anger and odd.

And he would be surprised that's Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is doing.

And how could anybody do that?

So Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) writes him a letter.

He says: Go until you reach the Muslim armies at Al-Yarmook(أليرموك).

Al-Yarmook(أليرموك) is now in Jordan, so he's sending him back again.

Go until you reach the Muslim armies at Al-Yarmook(أليرموك) for they are distressed and they are causing distress.

The Muslims are having a hard time with the Romans.

Go and save them and then he says; And do not by any means return to the like of what you have done.

Do not do something like that again, giving him clear orders, do not do the like of what you have done again.

So it was a very sharp tone.

But when I said the ambivalence of the feeling of Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), he said; Because no one after the help of Allah can break the enemy like you.

Don't put yourself at risk.

Because no one can break the enemy of Allah like you.

And no one will relieve the distressed Muslims like you.

Our Muslim armies are distressed fighting the Romans.

No one can relieve that distress but you.

So take care of yourself.

And then he says: Congratulations, Abu Sulaiman(أبوسليمان) on your intentions and your favorite position.

Now it's time for the Khalifah(خليفه) to congratulate Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) for the status that he has achieved.

Therefore complete your work so that Allah may make it complete for you.

Finish your work.

Your role is not over yet, so that Allah will even raise you further up.

Do not by any means let self admiration enter you.

See Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) was not only a leader for them was not only the Khalifah(خليفه) he was a fatherly figure for all of the Sahabah(صحابه).

He was a scholar, he was their Shaikh(شيخ) because he was the closest one to Rasool Allah ﷺ.

And Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) at that time was in his 60s and he was the most knowledgeable.

So, the relationship was not that of a politician to one of his Cabinet members it was a relationship of an older brother.

So he's giving them advice.

I mean, you would find it amazing, he's sending out this army and he's telling the leader of the army have Khushoo(خشوع) in Salah(صلاة).

You know teachings like this, that are usually given by a teacher to the student, but that was the relationship of Al-Khalifah(خليفه) to his followers. He said;

Do not by any means let self admiration enter you because Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is at such a high status.

Al-Khalifah(خليفه) wants to make sure that his heart is clean.

That Shaytan(شَيْطَانْ) does not get into his heart.

Do not by any means let self admiration enter you, so that you lose and fall.

See that you do not rely upon any works of yours, for Allah controls the bestowal of favor and He is the owner of rewards.

Don't let Ujb(عجب) enter your heart and don't depend on your deeds depends on Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ.

So, the letter reaches to Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) and he is told to leave Iraq(عراق) and go back to Ash-Sham(ألشام), Al Yarmook(أليرموك), Jordan.

So now Khalid(خالد) was told by Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) to split the army between him and Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa(ألمثنى بن حارثه).

Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) now is going to lead the armies of Iraq, while Khalid(خالد) leaves with half of the troops to Ash-Sham(ألشام).

So Khalid(خالد) splits the army into two.

And what he does is, he puts all of the companions of Rasool Allah ﷺ in his half.

Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) goes to him and said: Listen, I'm not gonna accept this half that you gave me.

You take all of the companions of Rasool Allah ﷺ with you, I'm not gonna allow that to happen.

So Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) I mean, they have the same number of forces.

But even though it was past the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ, they would still fighting of what Rasool Allah ﷺ, left them with.

He was the one, who gave them the ammunition for all of this.

So the Fatuhaat(فتوحات) that happened the time of Abu Bakr(ابوبكر), and that happened in a time of Umar(عُمَر), were just a product of the Tarbiyat(تربيعة) of Rasool Allah ﷺ,

one Sahabi(صحابي) counts like an entire army.

Rasool Allah ﷺ trained them in Madina.

And the Persian Empire and Roman Empire, they didn't care about Madina, many of them didn't even know what Madina was?

But they didn't know that the seeds of their destruction were planted in Madina, that Rasool Allah ﷺ even though he was miles and miles away from them,

he was raising up in the poor quarters of Madina, the ones, who will spread light to the corners of the world.

So Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) is saying I'm not going to allow you to take these.

So, Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) is giving him one companion after another.

Until he pleased him.

And then he moved on to Ash-Sham(ألشام).

And that's another adventure that we're going to talk about later.

Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى), see Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى), again, we said what was his opinion in the time of Rasool Allah ﷺ and how it changed in the time of Abu Bakr(ابوبكر)?

Because of Islam! He talks about that himself. He says, Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) said: I have fought against the Arabs and Al-Ajam(ألعجم), in Jahiliyyah(جَاهلِيَّة) and Islam.

Al-Ajam(ألعجم) are the non Arabs.

He said: I fight with them in Islam and before Islam, he says: It used to be that 100 of Al-Ajam(ألعجم) were stronger than 1000 of the Arabs.

But now 100 of the Arabs are stronger than 1000 of Al-Ajam(ألعجم) because of Islam.

And then he says: So don't let their numbers strike fear in your hearts.

And don't let their tall Lance's, spears and powerful bows intimidate you.

Because if they lose them, or if their equipment is taken away from them, they turn into cattle that you could chase away however you want.

He is saying that the disbeliever without his equipment is like cattle take him out of the cockpit and he is done.

So, Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa(ألمثنى بن حارثه) is giving here a very strong note to the Muslims, telling them that the numbers should not have intimidate you,

nor the equipment that they have.

Because in terms of numbers, and in terms of Uddah(عدة), preparation, they were way stronger than the Muslims.

Ibn Qayyim(إبن ألقيم) says, that the Romans and the Persians had more numbers and had more equipment and they're well built while their opponents were slim and thin.

I mean, we say that Umar Ibn Al-Khattab(عمرابن الخطاب) was tall and Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد) was tall, but in general these were people, who came out of the desert.

So in terms of the stature, definitely the armies of the Romans were stronger built than them.

But then Ibn Al-Qayyim(إبن ألقيم) says, But their hearts failed them, when they needed them most.

So, these big bodies don't have a strong heart and their hearts failed them when they needed them most.

So the Muslim should not fear all of these worldly calculations that we have in terms of numbers and equipment and all that stuff because it's meaningless.

I mean, there's something called Al-Wahn(ألوهن), weakness.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ can put Wahn(ألوهن) in the heart of somebody, whose fingers are on buttons of the most powerful weapon on the face of the earth,

but he will not be able to function it.

Because Allah has put Wahn(ألوهن) in his heart.

Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ talks about the Battle of Rasool Allah ﷺ with Al-Yahood(أليهود), Allah cast fear in their hearts, they had the strongest forts,

but Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ when he put fear in their hearts, their force did not help, their weapons did not help and their numbers did not help.

And Allahعَزَّوَجَلْ is the One, Who controls the hearts and He can put Wahn(ألوهن) or Ro'ub(رعب) in any heart. Rasool Allah ﷺ says: I was given victory a distance of a month through fear.

Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) was now given the sole authority over the forces in Iraq.

So, he was the leader there.

Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa Ash-Shaibani(ألمثنى بن حارثه شعيباني), was such a great leader and general it's a name that you must remember.

He was the one, who played a very important role in Iraq, in opening Iraq and he continued with Al-Fatoohaat(ألفتوحات) in Al-Iraq(ألعراق), in the absence of Khalid Ibn Walid(خالد ابن وليد).

So, he needed some reinforcements because he was getting deep into the territory of the enemy.

He sends a letter to Abu Bakr As-Siddique رضي الله عنه.

But Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) was busy with a more important priority at the time and that was the conquest of the Holy Land.

So Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) delayed his response to Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى), he was busy.

When Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) saw that he didn't get back a response from the Khalifah(خليفه).

He decided that he's going to go himself and meet with the Khalifah(خليفه).

So he leaves Iraq and it goes to Madina and he meets with the Khalifah(خليفه) and explains to him the situation, the Khalifah(خليفه) doesn't have anybody to give him.

Al-Khalifah(خليفه) has mobilized and squeezed, the tribes for all of their fighting forces and sent them to the Holy Land.

So Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) said: Then reinforced me with the Muslims, the ex Murtaddeen(مرتدين).

Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) was on his deathbed at that time.

So for his entire Khilafah(خِلَافَه), he has refused to allow Murtaddeen(مرتدين) to join.

Now since things are different, Al-Murtaddeen(ألمرتدين) have stood firm on Islam, he attested them for two years, Abu Bakr As-Siddique(أبوبكرالصديق) considered it.

So he told Umar(عُمَر), who was next to him.

He said: O Umar(عُمَر), Listen O Umar(عُمَر) to what I say to you, then act according to it.

I hope to die on this day of mine.

If I die, do not by any means let the evening enter before you have summon the men to go with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى) if I delay, until the night do not by any means,

let the morning come before you summon the men to go with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى).

Do not let any catastrophe at all even if it is great, keep you from the matter of your religion and your Lord's counsel.

You saw what I did, on the day of the Messenger of Allah.

See Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is telling Umar(عُمَر): Do not let any catastrophe hold you back from fulfilling your duties towards Allah and His messenger, he's alluding to his death.

He is saying: Even if I die, don't let that hold you back from mobilizing the forces on the same day I die and sending them out with Al-Muthanna(ألمثنى).

Subhaan Allah(سُبْحَان الله) Abu Bakr(ابوبكر) is not even willing to give a break.

And then he said: You saw what I did on the day the Messenger of Allah died and the people were never stricken with the like of it.

I mean, you saw what I did on that day that is when the Khalifah(خليفه) was given Baiyah(بَيْعة) to.

Three days after that I'm sending out the army of Osamah(أسامة).

So the death of Rasool Allah ﷺ was much greater catastrophe than my death.

Did not hold me back from fulfilling my duties.

So I want you O Umar(عُمَر) to follow my way.

Then he says: By Allah! If I were to weaken in the affair of Allah and the affair of His Messenger, He would abandon me and punish me so that Madina would be consumed in fire.

If Allah grants victory to the commanders in Syria.

Return the troops of Khalid(خالد) to Iraq, for they are its people, the governors of its affair alone, and the people of violence and courage against the enemy.

He says: If we finished with the affair of the Holy Land, send the people of Iraq back to Iraq.

That's their land and they are the people of courage and violence against their enemy.

So Al-Muthanna Bin Harissa Ash-Shaibani(ألمثنى بن حارثه شعيباني) was reinforced.
